name: Mike McCue
profile: American tech entrepreneur who never attended college: founded Paper Software (sold to Netscape for $20M in 1996), co-founded voice-browser Tellme Networks (acquired by Microsoft in 2007), then co-founded the Flipboard news-magazine app in 2010, which he still leads and has pushed into the open social web/fediverse.
interesting_fact: He gave up a congressional nomination to the US Air Force Academy to support his family after his father died, joined IBM on a six-month temp contract in 1986 and stayed three and a half years.
deep_cut_fact: His Netscape project to turn Navigator into a web-based desktop OS was codenamed 'Constellation' after a boat his father helped restore; he later bought a 48-foot classic wooden sailboat and named it Constellation too. His first app was a space-shuttle flight simulator written in TI-BASIC in 1981.
notes: Media-friendly; frequent podcast guest on the open social web. Press contact is the 'Contact Us' link on Flipboard's press page.
